newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Sol Melia slides on S&P rating.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Sol Melia slides on S&P rating.

text.p: Shares in Spain's Sol Melia slipped off morning highs on Wednesday after Standard & Poor's assigned the hotel chain a "BBB plus" rating.
Traders said the market had initially interpreted the rating as inadequate for the highly successful hotel chain, but they expected shares to rebound shortly.
"This initial negative reaction will be short-lived, especially since other hotel groups do not have ratings, so analysts are not used to looking at them in that light," one dealer said.

By 1145 GMT, shares were trading down 0.18 percent at 5,560 pesetas after trading around highs of 5,680 before S&P's announcement. Meanwhile, the Ibex-35 index of leading shares was trading up 1.12 percent at 6,872.89.
S&P said the rating was the highest the U.S.-based agency had awarded to corporates dedicated solely to the hotel business.
Sol Melia is Spain's leading hotel chain, managing 210 hotels in 25 countries, ranking it third in Europe.
S&P said the chain had a stable outlook given that it was expected to maintain a high level of profits and cash-flow based on its steady market share in Spain.
